newsitem.title: USA: Two men say they saw Tupac Shakur killers - paper.
newsitem.headline: Two men say they saw Tupac Shakur killers - paper.

text.p: Two men who claimed to have seen the gunmen who murdered rap star Tupac Shakur say they were never asked by police to view pictures of possible suspects in the unsolved case, the Los Angeles Times reported on Friday.
They said they informed Las Vegas investigators of what they saw after Shakur was shot in Las Vegas on Sept. 7, 1996, and said they were willing to cooperate with police, the newspaper said.

The comments by the two men, who were in a car behind the one in which the rapper and movie actor was riding, directly conflicted with charges by Las Vegas police that their investigation was thwarted by uncooperative witnesses.

The Times identified the men as Malcolm Greenridge, a member of Shakur's back-up quartet who performs under the stage name E.D.I. Mean, and Frank Alexander, Shakur's bodyguard. Alexander told the newspaper he saw the face of the shooter and Greenridge said he saw all four men in the car from which the fatal shots were fired.

Las Vegas police disputed their account of what they told police the night of the murder, but they told the Times the accounts could lead to a breakthrough in the case. They immediately placed a call to one of the witnesses and asked the Times to help in tracing the other.
New York lawyer Richard Fischbein, who represents Shakur's mother Afeni Shakur, told the Times she hoped police would contact the two men and show them a lineup of suspects.
"Even Inspector Clouseau would do that at this point," Fischbein told the newspaper, referring to the bumbling detective played by Peter Sellers in the "Pink Panther" movies.
